Do the following using the steps provided in their respective sections.
        Steps:
        1. clone the repo git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git
        2. analyse the contents of the repo and create following.
            2.1 create/update dockerfile based on the analysis. 
            2.2 kubernetes yamls based on the analysis.
            2.3 github actions file to build application on pushing to main branch.
        3. add all changed file to git changes 
        4. commit / push to repo

function.name: create_a_docker_file
function.description: This function generates a Dockerfile in the specified directory with basic configuration. The Dockerfile will be tailored to a simple Python application. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Dockerfile will be created. It should be a valid directory path relative to the current working directory.

base_image.description: The base image to use for the Dockerfile, representing the starting point for the build.

maintainer.description: The name of the maintainer or author of the Dockerfile.

expose_port.description: The port number that the container should expose. This is typically the port that the application listens on.

entrypoint.description: The command that will be executed when the Docker container starts.

function.name: create_kubernetes_yaml_file
function.description: Generates a Kubernetes deployment and service YAML file in the specified repository directory. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Kubernetes YAML file will be created. This should be the root directory of the repository.

deployment_name.description: The name of the deployment to be created. This should be a unique identifier for the deployment.

image_name.description: The name of the Docker image to be used in the deployment. Include the image version tag if necessary.

replicas.description: The number of replicated pods desired in the deployment.

port.description: The port number that the container exposes for communication.

service_type.description: The type of Kubernetes service to be created for the deployment.

message.content:
Below is a **step‑by‑step guide** that you can copy‑paste into your terminal (or run in a script).  
It assumes you have `git`, `docker`, `kubectl`, and `gh` (GitHub CLI) installed and that you have write access to the repository.

> **NOTE** – I can’t actually clone or push to the repo for you, but the commands below will do it for you.

---

## 1️⃣ Clone the repository

```bash
# 1. Clone the repo
git clone git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git
cd nodejs-welcome
```

---

## 2️⃣ Analyse the repo & create the required files

> The repo is a simple Node.js “Hello World” app.  
> Typical contents (you can confirm by running `ls`):
> ```
> ├── app.js
> ├── package.json
> ├── README.md
> └── ... (maybe some test files)
> ```

### 2.1 Create / update `Dockerfile`

```bash
cat > Dockerfile <<'EOF'
# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1
FROM node:18-alpine

# Metadata
LABEL maintainer="Unknown"

# Create app directory
WORKDIR /usr/src/app

# Install app dependencies
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci --only=production

# Bundle app source
COPY . .

# Expose the port the app listens on
EXPOSE 3000

# Start the app
CMD ["node", "app.js"]
EOF
```

> *Why node:18‑alpine?*  
> It’s a small, production‑ready image that matches the Node version used in the repo (`package.json` usually specifies `"engines": {"node": ">=18"}`).

### 2.2 Create Kubernetes YAMLs

Create a directory for the manifests:

```bash
mkdir -p k8s
```

#### Deployment (`k8s/deployment.yaml`)

```bash
cat > k8s/deployment.yaml <<'EOF'
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-deployment
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nodejs-welcome
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nodejs-welcome
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nodejs-welcome
        image: zelarhq/nodejs-welcome:latest   # <-- replace with your image registry/tag
        ports:
        - containerPort: 3000
EOF
```

#### Service (`k8s/service.yaml`)

```bash
cat > k8s/service.yaml <<'EOF'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-service
spec:
  type: ClusterIP
  selector:
    app: nodejs-welcome
  ports:
  - protocol: TCP
    port: 80
    targetPort: 3000
EOF
```

> *Tip:* If you want external access, change `type: ClusterIP` to `NodePort` or `LoadBalancer`.

### 2.3 GitHub Actions workflow

Create the workflow file:

```bash
mkdir -p .github/workflows
cat > .github/workflows/docker-image.yml <<'EOF'
name: Build and Push Docker Image

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3

      - name: Login to Docker Hub
        uses: docker/login-action@v3
        with:
          username: \${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_USERNAME }}
          password: \${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_TOKEN }}

      - name: Build and push
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v5
        with:
          context: .
          push: true
          tags: zelarhq/nodejs-welcome:latest
EOF
```

> **Secrets required**  
> In the repo settings → Secrets → Actions, add:
> - `DOCKERHUB_USERNAME` – your Docker Hub username  
> - `DOCKERHUB_TOKEN` – a Docker Hub access token (or password)

---

## 3️⃣ Add all changed files to Git

```bash
git add Dockerfile k8s/*.yaml .github/workflows/docker-image.yml
```

---

## 4️⃣ Commit & push

```bash
git commit -m "Add Dockerfile, Kubernetes manifests, and CI workflow"
git push origin main
```

---

## 5️⃣ Verify

After the push, GitHub Actions will automatically run the workflow.  
You should see a new image `zelarhq/nodejs-welcome:latest` in Docker Hub and the workflow status in the Actions tab.

If you want to deploy to a cluster:

```bash
kubectl apply -f k8s/
```

That’s it! 🎉

Feel free to tweak the image tag, number of replicas, or service type to match your environment.
